response.sql: WITH j AS (SELECT e.ordersmark, o.timespan, e.fillcount FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON e.ordersmark = o.recordvault), t AS (SELECT timespan, AVG(fillcount) AS tif_avg FROM j GROUP BY timespan), p AS (SELECT ordersmark, timespan, AVG(fillcount) AS avg_fill FROM j GROUP BY ordersmark, timespan), r AS (SELECT p.ordersmark, p.timespan, p.avg_fill, p.avg_fill - t.tif_avg AS excess_over_tif, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.timespan ORDER BY p.avg_fill DESC NULLS LAST) AS rnk FROM p JOIN t ON t.timespan IS p.timespan WHERE p.avg_fill > t.tif_avg) SELECT ordersmark, timespan, avg_fill, excess_over_tif, rnk FROM r WHERE rnk <= 3 ORDER BY timespan, rnk, ordersmark

assumptions.assumption: orders.recordvault is unique per order (documented as a unique order reference), so the join does not duplicate executions.
The time-in-force average is computed over matched executions only (unmatched dropped), averaging non-null fillcount values with each execution weighted equally.
Ranking is applied among orders that pass the above-average filter; this gives the same ranks as ranking all orders, since the kept orders are the highest ones in each group.
